description: The 2010 Population and Housing Census Report of the Virgin Islands (British) is a PDF of 130 pages. The copy read here is hosted by the UN Statistics Division, because the government page for the report now returns 404. The census counted 10,830 households and 28,054 persons, with fieldwork running from August 2010 to July 2012 after hurricanes and other delays. Household tables give the type of building, outer wall material and period built, and show that 59.8 percent of Anegada households lived in wood or mixed-material houses against 8.3 percent on Tortola. Water tables split public street water (48.7 percent) from private cisterns (32.3 percent), both combined, catchments, and springs or wells. Toilet tables separate flush toilets linked to the sewer (24.8 percent) from septic tanks. Lighting tables count public electricity, private generators and solar, and an amenity table counts water pumps, generators, water heaters, air conditioners and internet connections. Coverage is all inhabited islands, with most tables by island. Format and access: free PDF, no registration. Licence: none found. Caveats: only about 83 percent of persons were enumerated in the field and the report adjusted the rest; tables are printed, not machine-readable; no newer census report was found. Simulation uses: wall materials and cistern reliance for hurricane and drought exposure by island, and sewer versus septic shares for wastewater planning. Related records: none closer in the catalogue.

schema_summary: Household tables 1 to 63: 7-8 type of building (residential, residential and commercial) by island; 9-10 outer wall material (wood, concrete, stone and mixes) by island; 11 year or period building built from before 1980; 12-13 dwelling unit type; 14-19 tenure, insurance, land arrangement; 20-21 cooking fuel; 22-23 garbage disposal (bin, public or private truck, dumping, burning); 24-27 water supply and drinking water (public piped street water, private cistern, both, truck, catchments, spring or well); 28-29 toilet linked to sewer or septic tank, pit latrine; 32-33 lighting (public electricity, private generator, solar, kerosene); 34-41 rooms and overcrowding; 42-43 amenities (air conditioner, water pump, water heater, generator, fixed phone, internet, cable, satellite dish, vehicle) by island; 44-51 environmental issues. Person tables 64 onward cover demography, migration, education, work and income.
